_help.whatThisFileIs: The list of accounts that may open the hidden staff panel (Left Alt + F2), which covers the release preview, the Verified Creator and Verified Community application review tools, the verification withdrawal tool, and hiring. It is a plain public file, so it must never contain passwords, tokens, email addresses, or anything private. Only public profile details belong here.
_help.whatItIsNot: This is not a login service. The site has no backend and does not contact Discord, so an entry here cannot prove who someone is. It is an allowlist that keeps the panel out of casual hands, nothing more. Never put anything confidential behind it: the panel only changes what one browser displays.

fields.username: Discord username, without the @. Matched case-insensitively. Required unless you only use userId.
fields.displayName: Optional. The name shown in the panel once signed in.
fields.userId: Optional. A Discord user ID (the long number) or a Yapin user ID (a UUID such as 8a2c94c1-de91-4e73-a425-dfd178c390dc). Also accepted at sign-in, and useful when someone renames.
fields.role: Required. One of: owner, admin, maintainer, editor, viewer. Higher ranks can do everything the lower ones can, plus one more thing each. Unknown or missing roles are treated as viewer.
fields.enabled: Optional. Set to false to keep an account in the list but block it.
fields.codeHash: Optional. A PBKDF2-SHA256 value of the form pbkdf2-sha256$600000$<salt>$<key>, or a legacy lowercase hex SHA-256 left over from an older file. Leave it as an empty string to allow the account on its name alone.

ranks.viewer: Read only. Opens the panel and sees the published release, but every field is disabled.
ranks.editor: Can preview release changes in the browser, and download or copy the release.json they produce.
ranks.maintainer: Everything editor can do, plus replacing their own staff code.
ranks.admin: Everything maintainer can do, plus replacing any staff code except the owner's, reviewing Verified Creator and Verified Community applications, and withdrawing a verification.
ranks.owner: Everything admin can do, plus hiring new accounts and replacing the owner's own code. Keep exactly one owner.

_help.howToHire: Only an account with role owner can hire. Sign in as the owner, fill in the new person's details, press Hire staff account, then re-enter the owner username and staff code. A different account or a wrong code is refused. The generated code is shown once; only its hash belongs in this file. The panel also generates the introduction to send: it uses the username or an optional first/public name and optional pronouns, and always writes rank, age, and favorites as Not Disclosed. Never ask for a last or middle name, address, phone number, IP address, Social Security number, or driver's license or state ID number.
howToReplaceACode: A hash cannot be turned back into a code, by anyone. A forgotten or leaked code is replaced, not recovered.
1. Sign in to the panel with any working code.
2. Open "Replace a staff code", enter the username or user ID, and press "Generate new code".
3. Do it for your own account with any rank from maintainer up. Replacing someone else's code needs admin or owner; the owner's own code can only be replaced by the owner.
4. Copy the new code and send it to the person privately. It is shown once and never stored.
5. Copy the new codeHash, or the whole account entry, and paste it over that account's block here.
6. Upload this file. The old code stops working once the new hash is published.
howToAddAnAccount: 1. Open the site and press Left Alt + F2, then sign in with the account whose role is owner. Only that account can hire.
2. Open "New staff account", enter the new person's Discord username, display name, user ID, and role, and press "Hire staff account".
3. Re-enter the owner username and owner staff code to confirm. A different account or a wrong code is refused.
4. Copy the account entry. Copy the staff code too and give it to the person privately; it is shown once and is never stored.
5. Open this file in a text editor and paste the entry after the last account inside the "accounts" square brackets.
6. Put a comma after the closing brace of the account that came before it.
7. Save the file and upload it to the repository at assets/data/staff.json. The codeHash in the entry is the only part that belongs here.
8. From then on the person signs in with that username or user ID plus the staff code you gave them.
howToSetAStaffCode: 1. For a new account, "New staff account" generates the code and the codeHash together. Copy the entry it produces.
2. For an existing account, use "Replace a staff code": it generates a new code and its derivation in one step.
3. Or open "Derive a codeHash from a code", type a code you have chosen, and press "Derive codeHash".
4. Copy the whole result. It looks like pbkdf2-sha256$600000$<salt>$<key> and is longer than 64 characters.
5. Paste it into that account's codeHash field in this file, in quotes, and upload the file.
6. A long, unique code is the only kind worth using, because this file is public and the value can be attacked offline. Generated codes are six words plus four digits.
howToWithdrawAVerification: A badge that has already been sent cannot be deleted or recalled. Withdrawal ends the permission to use it and makes the verification ID invalid.
1. Sign in as an admin or owner and open "Withdraw a verification".
2. Enter the verification ID (RFCU-VC-... for a creator, RFCU-VCM-... for a community), choose the program, and add the recipient name and the project or community name.
3. Optionally add a reason, press "Generate withdrawal message", and copy the message.
4. Send it to the recipient yourself. The site stores no revocation list, so keep a private record of every withdrawal.
5. The message tells the recipient to take the badge down. It does not remove copies that already exist.
_help.beforeYouPublish: Replace or remove the placeholder account below. Leaving a name-only account enabled means anyone who reads this file can open the panel.
